name: The Jewel House
summary: The household's plate on a stepped buffet, a strong cupboard behind an iron lattice, iron-bound chests against brick-lined walls, and a jeweller's casket.
description: A Burgundian lord kept his wealth where it could be admired and counted. On the stepped buffet against the north wall the gilt plate stands tier above tier under a green dosser: cups, standing dishes, a ewer, everything the household would bring out for a feast and then carry back here under guard. The strong cupboard beside it is oak behind a lattice of iron straps with a lock the size of a hand. To the south the walls are lined in brick, the century's new fire-proof material, and the chests in front of them are bound in iron; a jeweller's table holds a casket, and sacks of coin sit on the floor as if nobody had got round to counting them. Somebody has.
build: Shell: the kit's Keep shell, 12.0 × 12.0 × 0.30 m slab, 0.50 m dressed-sandstone walls 4.60 m clear, a 0.45 m madder trim course, an archway 2.60 × 3.31 m centred on every wall.
Stepped buffet (NE): three oak tiers 2.40 m wide against the north wall, centred x 3.60: 0.90 deep × 0.90 m, then 0.60 deep × 0.45 m, then 0.30 deep × 0.45 m; tier tops at 1.20 / 1.65 / 2.10 m.
Plate: three gilt cups on the first tier, two gilt dishes 0.30 m standing on edge on the second, a gilt ewer 0.34 m and two cups on the third.
Dosser: a verdure wool panel 2.60 × 1.60 m on the north wall above the buffet, from 2.10 m.
Strong cupboard (NW): oak 1.60 × 0.60 × 2.20 m against the north wall at x −3.60; four vertical and four horizontal iron straps 0.04 m over its doors, a steel lock plate.
Brick lining (south wall): two brick panels 3.40 × 2.40 m, centred x ±3.60, 0.04 m thick.
Iron-bound chests: oak 1.20 × 0.70 × 0.70 m at (±3.40, −5.00), an iron lid band and three iron straps over each.
Jeweller's table (SE): oak 0.90 × 0.60 m, top 0.80 m at (4.40, −2.90); a casket 0.30 × 0.20 × 0.20 m with a gilt lid on its east half.
Light: an iron pricket candle stand 1.50 m at (1.95, 4.00), by the buffet.
sockets: Archway ×4, centred on each wall: 2.60 × 3.31 m (Keep), all open
Buffet tiers: loot anchors on the first (1.20 m) and second (1.65 m) tiers
Chest lids and the jeweller's table: loot anchors

gameplay: Five loot anchors: the richest Late keep room, plate in full view on the buffet.
The strong cupboard is scenery with a lock on it: it promises more than it holds.
The chests sit against the south wall, so a thief looting them has their back to the north archway.
